dedupe_keys.name: pytradeshifts network model of food trade shifts under yield shocks

description: PyTradeShifts is a Python network model that estimates how international food trade flows and trading communities change when crop yields fall. It builds the trade network for a crop from FAO data, removes re-exports with the Croft et al. (2018) algorithm so that each country exports no more than it produces, applies yield changes by country and recomputes flows, then detects trade communities and compares them before and after the shock, following Hedlund et al. (2022). The provider is the Alliance to Feed the Earth in Disasters (ALLFED), and the Earth System Dynamics article on food trade disruption after global catastrophes (2025) links to this code. Coverage is global at country level for the crops in FAO trade data. The code is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 licence, installs with uv and is driven from Jupyter notebooks; the latest tag read today is 1.3. Caveats: the model redistributes existing trade proportionally and does not represent prices, stocks or export bans explicitly, and results depend on the base year of FAO data. Simulation uses: stress tests of national food supply under multiple breadbasket failures, nuclear winter or volcanic scenarios, and identification of countries whose imports depend on few partners. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances and trade (data-faostat) supply the inputs, and the global food shock and trade model (model-global-food-shock-trade) adds prices.
